paragraphs.title: The Search for Territory and the Discovery of Laish

easy.explanation: The tribe of Dan sought an inheritance because it had not yet received all its territory.
easy.q: Which tribe was seeking an inheritance to dwell in?

easy.explanation: Dan sent five men from Zorah and Eshtaol.
easy.q: How many men did the children of Dan send to spy out the land?

easy.explanation: When they came to Mount Ephraim, they lodged at Micah’s house.
easy.q: Where did the five men lodge when they came to Mount Ephraim?

answers: To spy out and search the land
To meet the king of Zidon
medium.explanation: They were sent to spy out the land and search for a place to possess.
medium.q: Why did the children of Dan send the five men?

answers: They lived peacefully and without fear
medium.explanation: The people of Laish lived carelessly, quiet and secure.
medium.q: What does “quiet and secure” describe about the people of Laish?

answers: It was crowded and strongly fortified
It was quiet, isolated, and prosperous
medium.explanation: They saw a quiet people in a large land where there was no want of anything.
medium.q: What did the spies discover about Laish?

answers: Their search for territory led them to investigate a suitable place
They were looking only for a place for a priest
challenge.explanation: Because their inheritance had not fully fallen to them, they searched for land to possess.
challenge.q: How was Dan’s lack of an inheritance related to sending the spies?

answers: Its people were isolated and had no business with other people
challenge.explanation: Laish was far from the Zidonians and had no business with any man.
challenge.q: Which detail made Laish seem like an easy place to conquer?

answers: He told them to remain at Micah’s house
He told them to go in peace and encouraged their way
challenge.explanation: The priest said, “Go in peace,” and told them that their way was before the Lord.
challenge.q: What does the priest’s answer show about the encouragement the spies received?

paragraphs.title: The Departure of the Six Hundred Warriors

easy.explanation: Six hundred men appointed with weapons of war went out.
easy.q: How many armed men went out from the family of the Danites?

easy.explanation: They went up and pitched in Kirjathjearim in Judah.
easy.q: Where did the Danites camp on the way?

answers: An ephod, teraphim, graven image, and molten image
easy.explanation: The spies identified these four objects in the house.
easy.q: What objects did the five spies identify in Micah’s house?

medium.explanation: They returned to Micah’s house and took the objects the spies had identified.
medium.q: What did the Danites do after returning to Micah’s house?

medium.explanation: The six hundred men were prepared and armed for war.
medium.q: What does “appointed with weapons of war” mean?

answers: The spies stayed at Laish while the warriors returned
They all left without taking anything
The spies took the objects while the warriors stood at the entrance
medium.explanation: The five men entered to take the objects, while the armed men stood by the gate.
medium.q: How did the five spies and the six hundred warriors work together?

answers: The spies already knew about the objects there
challenge.explanation: The spies knew that Micah’s house contained the ephod, teraphim, and images.
challenge.q: Why did the Danites return to Micah’s house after camping at Kirjathjearim?

answers: They provided force and protection during the taking of the objects
They waited for the priest’s answer
challenge.explanation: Their presence gave the spies military support while they entered the house.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the six hundred warriors standing at the gate?

answers: The objects were taken, Dan departed, and the army camped at Kirjathjearim
The army camped at Kirjathjearim, Dan departed, and the objects were taken
Dan departed, camped at Kirjathjearim, returned to Micah’s house, and took the objects
challenge.explanation: The Danites first departed, then camped at Kirjathjearim, and afterward returned to Micah’s house.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

paragraphs.title: The Taking of the Shrine Objects and the Priest’s Departure

answers: The graven image, ephod, teraphim, and molten image
easy.explanation: These are the objects named in the passage.
easy.q: Which objects did the Danites take from Micah’s house?

easy.explanation: The Danites persuaded the priest to go with them.
easy.q: Who joined the children of Dan?

answers: The little ones, cattle, and carriage
easy.explanation: They placed the little ones, cattle, and carriage before them.
easy.q: What did the Danites put before them as they traveled?

answers: They offered him service to a tribe and a family
They asked him to remain with Micah
medium.explanation: They asked whether it was better to serve one man’s house or a tribe and family in Israel.
medium.q: How did the Danites persuade the priest to join them?

medium.explanation: The carriage refers to the belongings and baggage carried by the traveling group.
medium.q: What does “carriage” mean in this passage?

answers: He received a city of his own
He accepted a broader position among the tribe of Dan
medium.explanation: He preferred being a priest to a tribe and family rather than to one man’s house.
medium.q: Why was the priest’s heart glad?

answers: He moved from serving Micah’s household to serving an entire tribe
He became one of the six hundred warriors
challenge.explanation: The Danites offered him service to a tribe and family in Israel.
challenge.q: What caused the change in the priest’s position?

answers: They were moving to settle in a new place
They were only checking the road
They left their families at Micah’s house
challenge.explanation: The group was traveling with families, animals, and possessions as part of a settlement.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the little ones, cattle, and carriage being led before the Danites?

answers: The priest joined, the objects were returned, and Dan departed
The objects were taken, the priest joined, and the group continued
Micah joined them, and the objects were returned
challenge.explanation: The Danites took the objects, persuaded the priest to join them, and then continued their journey.
challenge.q: What was the main sequence of actions?

answers: Micah and the people near his house
easy.explanation: The men near Micah’s house gathered together and overtook the Danites.
easy.q: Who overtook the children of Dan after they left Micah’s house?

answers: That they give him an inheritance
That they return his objects and priest
easy.explanation: Micah said they had taken away his gods and priest.
easy.q: What did Micah demand from the Danites?

easy.explanation: When Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he went back home.

answers: The Danites were too strong for him
The priest told him to withdraw
medium.explanation: Micah realized that he could not oppose the stronger Danite force.

answers: They called out loudly to them
medium.explanation: They called out to the Danites as they pursued them.
medium.q: What does it mean that the men “cried” unto the children of Dan?

answers: They threatened him and his household
medium.explanation: They warned that angry fellows might attack him and cost him his life.
medium.q: How did the Danites respond to Micah’s demand?

answers: Micah was stronger than the Danites
The Danites had a clear advantage in strength
challenge.explanation: Micah turned back after seeing that the Danites were too strong for him.
challenge.q: What does the confrontation reveal about the balance of power?

answers: Micah abandoned the pursuit and returned home
challenge.explanation: The threat caused Micah to realize that he could not resist them.
challenge.q: What was the practical result of the Danites’ threat?

answers: Micah overtook them, demanded his things, the Danites threatened him, and he withdrew
The Danites overtook Micah, returned the objects, and he withdrew
Micah joined the Danites and continued north
challenge.explanation: Micah caught up with them, made his demand, was threatened, and then returned home.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the confrontation?

paragraphs.title: The Conquest of Laish and the Founding of Dan

easy.explanation: The Danites came against Laish and attacked its people.
easy.q: Which city did the Danites attack?

easy.explanation: The passage says that they burned the city with fire.
easy.q: What did the Danites do to the city after smiting its inhabitants?

easy.explanation: They called the city Dan after Dan their father.
easy.q: What name did the Danites give the city?

answers: It was far from Zidon and had no business with other people
Its people asked to fight Dan
medium.explanation: Laish was isolated, far from Zidon, and had no connection with others.
medium.q: Why was there no deliverer for Laish?

answers: There was no water in the city
No one came to help its people
There was no house in the city
medium.explanation: Because of its isolation, no one came to rescue the people of Laish.
medium.q: What does “no deliverer” mean in this context?

answers: They built a city and dwelt therein
medium.explanation: Afterward they built a city and settled there.
medium.q: What did the Danites do after conquering the city?

answers: Its peace and isolation meant that no help came during the attack
Its wealth caused its people to attack Dan
Its nearness to Zidon brought an army to help
challenge.explanation: The city’s isolation, earlier seen as security, left it without a deliverer.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the earlier description of Laish and its conquest?

answers: After Dan, the father of the tribe
challenge.explanation: The passage says it was named after Dan their father.
challenge.q: Why was the city called Dan?

answers: Attacking, burning, building, and naming the city Dan
challenge.explanation: The Danites attacked and burned Laish, then built it and called it Dan.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

paragraphs.title: The Idol and the Shrine at Dan

easy.explanation: The Danites set up the graven image that Micah had made.
easy.q: What did the children of Dan set up in the city of Dan?

easy.explanation: Jonathan, the son of Gershom, and his sons served as priests.
easy.q: Who served as priests to the tribe of Dan?

easy.explanation: The passage says that the house of God was in Shiloh.
easy.q: Where was the house of God at that time?

answers: They left it on the road
They set it up among themselves at Dan
medium.explanation: They set up the image in the city of Dan.
medium.q: What did the Danites do with Micah’s graven image?

answers: The forced removal of the people from the land
medium.explanation: Captivity refers to the land and its people being taken or removed.
medium.q: What does “the captivity of the land” refer to?

answers: Until the day of the captivity of the land
medium.explanation: The passage says they served until the day of the captivity of the land.
medium.q: How long did Jonathan and his sons serve as priests to Dan?

answers: The graven image was at Dan, while the house of God was at Shiloh
The graven image was at Shiloh, while the house of God was at Dan
challenge.explanation: The final verse contrasts Micah’s graven image at Dan with the house of God at Shiloh.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the chapter?

answers: They became part of Dan’s place of worship
challenge.explanation: The Danites continued using the graven image after setting it up in Dan.
challenge.q: What does setting up the image at Dan show about the objects taken from Micah?

answers: The priests left, the image was returned, and the tabernacle moved to Dan
The tabernacle was established at Dan, and only afterward was the image set up
The Danites set up the image, Jonathan and his descendants served there, and the house of God was at Shiloh
challenge.explanation: These are the closing details given in the passage.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence at the end of the chapter?
